claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The report characterizes AI as having moved from assistant to author at scale, with humans moved into review and oversight rather than creation.
claims.quote: In the organizations we studied, AI has moved from a tool that assists engineers to one that authors code at scale, with humans increasingly in a review and oversight role rather than a creation role.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The report says survey-based findings capture developers feeling more productive at the individual level, because task completion is up and code is flowing faster.
claims.quote: DORA's  fi ndings are based on surveys. Surveys capture how developers feel about their work. And right now, developers feel more productive, because at the individual level, they are. Task completion is up. Code is  fl owing faster. The tools feel powerful.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The report states all organizations suffer the Acceleration Whiplash regardless of engineering maturity; strong pre-AI practices show the same quality degradation.
claims.quote: One  fi nding holds across all segments of data: All organizations suffer from the Acceleration Whiplash, irrespective of their engineering maturity. The organizations with strong pre-AI engineering practices see the same quality degradation as those without.
